title: When Tukey meets Chauvenet: a new boxplot criterion for outlier detection
When Tukey meets Chauvenet: a new boxplot criterion for outlier detection
summary: The paper addresses the fact that Tukey’s boxplot uses one-size-fits-all fences while Chauvenet’s criterion is not robust to contaminated data. It fuses the two by expressing Tukey’s quartile fences through robust mean/SD estimates and setting the sample-size-adjusted coefficient k_n^Chau = Φ^{-1}(1-0.25/n)/1.35 - 0.5. In normal-data simulations with two contaminated points, the Chauvenet-type boxplot labels 2 total suspected outliers at n=500 (vs 3 for Tukey) and many fewer false positives at larger n, and it detects the 3 junior civil-service pay freezes in the real Hong Kong data.

    M = 397
    MATRIX_A = 0x9908B0DF

count_fences <- function(x, k) {
  q <- quantile(x, c(0.25, 0.75), type = 7)
  q1 <- unname(q[1]); q3 <- unname(q[2])
  iqr <- q3 - q1
  LF <- q1 - k * iqr
  UF <- q3 + k * iqr
  out <- (x < LF) | (x > UF)
  contam <- out[(length(x) - 1):length(x)]  # the two known contaminated points

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reproduce the normal-data outlier counts of Lin, Zhang & Tong (2025),
"When Tukey meets Chauvenet: a new boxplot criterion for outlier detection"
(arXiv:2506.06491), Section 4.1 / Figure 2, using the authors' released code.

Claims C1-C6: for N(0,1) samples of size n in {500, 5000, 50000} with the last
two observations replaced by the contaminated points 5 and 6 (set.seed(1863),
seed reset before each n, exactly as in the authors' Examples/Section4_normal.R),
count the total suspected outliers of (a) the Chauvenet-type boxplot with
k^Chau_n = qnorm(1 - 0.25/n)/1.35 - 0.5 (paper Eq. 9) and (b) Tukey's boxplot
(k = 1.5), where an observation is counted when it lies strictly outside
Q1 - k*IQR / Q3 + k*IQR and the two contaminated points are included in the
total.

Authoritative path (R installed, discovered on PATH or in standard Windows
locations): R 4.x + the authors' released ChauBoxplot package.  The fence
coefficient is transcribed verbatim from the released package source
(ChauBoxplot/R/chau_boxplot.R), and the quartile convention is stats::quantile
type 7 -- the statistic ggplot2's StatBoxplot (wrapped by the authors'
geom_chau_boxplot) uses, which is what produced Figure 2.  Cross-checks per n:
